title: Vector and Archive Anew
premise: Casper Voss has spent a decade hiding among cargo routes, but the discovery of her own name on the manifest of the Meridian—a ship that supposedly never flew—drags her into the fleet's buried history. The manifest is a key to the Archive, a relay at the edge of dead space holding the original backups of every crew member who 'died' in the Meridian incident, including Casper's first self. As the fleet truce expires and rival factions race to control or destroy the Archive, Casper must choose between erasing her past to stay free or claiming an inheritance that could reignite war. In the end she broadcasts the Archive openly to everyone, dissolving its power as a weapon, and accepts that identity is not a single stored self but the sum of choices made since.
about_author: Astrid Thackeray is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who traded shipping manifests for starship ones in her fiction. She writes about people caught between the records kept about them and the lives they actually live.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Casper Voss runs a routine haul through contested orbits, establishing her careful invisibility and her unease around the backup pods sleeping in the hold. POV: Casper. Beat: quiet dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: A customs clerk flags an anomaly: 'Casper Voss' listed on the Meridian, a ship officially lost before Casper was licensed. She realizes someone is using her real name—or her real past. POV: Casper. Beat: the floor drops out.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter as Casper burns her safehouses and contacts, retracing how she built her new identity after the Meridian incident. Her partner Dree notices the fear. POV: Casper. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: A fleet archivist named Ilem Sarn finds Casper at dock, offering protection in exchange for the manifest chip. He knows what sleeps in dead space—and what it costs to wake it. POV: Casper. Beat: temptation wrapped in menace.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper interrogates her own cargo AI, which has logged encrypted pings from the relay for years—signals addressed to her old designation. Someone has been calling her home. POV: Casper. Beat: grief surfacing through machinery.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: The fleet announces the contested-orbit truce expires in thirty days; factions begin arming. Casper realizes the Archive relay will be the first target once fighting starts. POV: Casper. Beat: stakes become a countdown.

chapters.title: Dree's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dree, revealed to have sold Casper's route data to survive, confesses—but also reveals the buyer's coordinates. Loyalty fractures against truth. POV: Dree. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness entangled.

chapters.title: Running the Contested Lanes
chapters.summary: A harrowing transit through patrol corridors, Casper smuggling herself toward dead space aboard a coffin ship. First glimpse of another faction racing her there. POV: Casper. Beat: momentum and isolation.

chapters.title: The First Backup
chapters.summary: At a derelict waystation, Casper finds a pre-Meridian backup of herself and speaks with a recording of who she was. The conversation is tender and unbearable. POV: Casper. Beat: identity as inheritance.

chapters.title: Sarn's Fleet
chapters.summary: Ilem Sarn's true allegiance emerges: he serves a faction that wants the Archive destroyed to bury the Meridian massacre. He offers Casper erasure instead of exposure. POV: Sarn. Beat: antagonist with a sympathetic logic.

chapters.title: Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Casper reaches the outer marker where navigation fails and the relay's beacon finally answers, guiding her in. The dead space is full of wrecks from the incident. POV: Casper. Beat: awe and horror.

chapters.title: The Archive Wakes
chapters.summary: Inside the relay, thousands of backups stir at her arrival—including the original Casper Voss, who remembers everything Casper has spent ten years forgetting. POV: Original Casper. Beat: confrontation with the self she fled.

chapters.title: Two Navigators
chapters.summary: Original and current Casper negotiate over one body, one name, one future. The debate becomes the book's thematic heart: which self is real? POV: alternating. Beat: intimate philosophical duel.

chapters.title: Signal Intercepted
chapters.summary: Sarn's faction arrives with weapons hot; a rival salvage syndicate follows. The relay becomes a three-way standoff with the truce hours from expiring. POV: Casper. Beat: trap closing.

chapters.title: Dree Returns
chapters.summary: Dree arrives uninvited with a stolen fleet code that can open the Archive's broadcast array—her way of repaying the betrayal. POV: Dree. Beat: loyalty redeemed at cost.

chapters.title: The Massacre File
chapters.summary: Casper accesses the Meridian's final logs: the fleet ordered the deaths and the backups secretly preserved as leverage. Truth reframes everything, including Sarn's mission. POV: Casper. Beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Sarn's Choice
chapters.summary: Confronted with proof his own family's backups are held here too, Sarn wavers between orders and conscience. A firefight breaks out anyway. POV: Sarn. Beat: the antagonist humanized.

chapters.title: Truce Expires
chapters.summary: Fleet warships jump into dead space as the ceasefire lapses. The relay takes damage; backups begin degrading. Casper must broadcast now or lose everyone forever. POV: Casper. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Casper opens the Archive to every ship, every faction, every citizen simultaneously—making the backups public property and useless as leverage. Climax of the theme: truth as disarmament. POV: Casper. Beat: defiant transcendence.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Dark
chapters.summary: In the ceasefire that shock forces, Casper negotiates amnesty by surrendering her hidden decade. The original Casper chooses to remain archived, at peace, no longer competing. POV: Original Casper. Beat: reconciliation between selves.

chapters.title: Manifest, Amended
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Casper signs a new manifest under her true name, legally resurrected. Dree joins her crew; Sarn sends a quiet message of thanks. POV: Casper. Beat: inheritance claimed, not escaped.

chapters.title: Vector Home
chapters.summary: Final chapter: a last haul through now-open orbits, the hold empty of secrets, the relay's signal a lighthouse behind her. Casper navigates forward without hiding. POV: Casper. Beat: earned peace and open horizon.
